correctness.rationale: All 77,520 seven-subsets and 125,970 eight-subsets are exhausted with monotone zero-forcing closure. No size-seven forcing set exists; exactly 13,520 size-eight sets do. The checker constructs every exchange edge, tests all 13,520 BFS sources and 91,388,440 unordered pairs, and asserts exact distance excess <=1, the 47,380 defect count by Johnson level, radius 7 and diameter 8. An independently constructed bipartite-Kneser checker confirms the host graph, minimum sets, all 178,560 edges, degrees, connectivity and nine BFS roots; a four-set explicit detour demonstrates strictness. Computation is an exhaustive finite proof, not an extrapolation.

originality.rationale: The prior Desargues forcing-number theorem gives the optimum seed size eight, and general reconfiguration literature defines and algorithmically enumerates exchange graphs but does not determine this host graph's exact all-pairs metric. Searches under Desargues, GP(10,3) and bipartite Kneser names found no matching 47,380-defect metric classification. Known configuration and connectivity counts are expressly not treated as novel; the exact one-step defect bound, defect locations and eccentricity refinement are not implied by them. value.rationale: Feasible transitions of minimum zero-forcing seeds are naturally compared with the unrestricted Johnson metric because both count one-for-one replacements. This complete finite metric classification proves that every pair is within one extra step of the unrestricted optimum, locates all 47,380 exceptional pairs by overlap size, and determines the nontrivial 980/12,540 eccentricity split. The known scalar Z and state/edge connectivity counts are prerequisites, not the claimed advance. The sharp obstruction structure and benchmark value justify this invariant independently of broader parameter-family generalization.
